title: Production Configuration Management knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Production Configuration Management”?
options: Checking whether a process is running
Calling the operating system's service-management interface
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Separating settings from code” under lesson 185, “Production Configuration Management”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Production Configuration Management”?
options: Design retries, cleanup, and concurrent operations around partial failure and recovery.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
questions.answer_key: Design retries, cleanup, and concurrent operations around partial failure and recovery.
questions.explanation: Design retries, cleanup, and concurrent operations around partial failure and recovery. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Production Configuration Management”?
options: Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
